body.estimand_functional: For a fixed explicit input \(I\), write \(\mathfrak M(I)=\{\mathcal M_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_{\mathcal L}\}\).  For every \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathcal L}\) with \(K(\theta)>0\), the causal target is \(q(\mathcal M_\theta)=H(\theta)/K(\theta)\).  If a verified rational circuit \(C\) is returned, then \(C(\Phi(\theta))=H(\theta)/K(\theta)\); uniform instance-relative identification need not imply that such a \(C\) exists.  On the obstruction instance, the unique identified value is the nonnegative root \(q=\sqrt{ab/c}\) of \(cq^2=ab\) on \(c>0\).

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite menu of complete observational and perfect-interventional regimes is supplied together with explicit finite source alphabets and a response decoder.  Symbolic identification is uniform over the full positive feasible image of the instance-relative family \(\mathfrak M(I)=\{\mathcal M_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_{\mathcal L}\}\), not over all mechanisms merely compatible with the graph bound.
sampling_model.units: For inference, regime \(r\) supplies \(n_r\) i.i.d. finite-alphabet draws, independently across regimes.
sampling_model.treatment: Each regime clamps a declared endogenous subset \(Z\) to \(z\) and records the complete joint outcome on \(V\setminus Z\).
sampling_model.overlap: Evaluation separates infeasible menu vectors from feasible vectors having no positive-denominator model.  Inference assumes positive limiting regime fractions and a fixed positive margin for every circuit divisor.  Its variance threshold satisfies \(\kappa_n\to0\) and \(\delta_n/\kappa_n\to0\); the proof establishes the simultaneous matrix rate \(\lVert\widehat\Sigma_Q-\Sigma_Q\rVert=O_P(\delta_n)=o_P(\kappa_n)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No infinite-dimensional nuisance is estimated.  Empirical multinomial cells pass through a verified rational circuit by automatic differentiation; symbolically constant coordinates are exact, and nonsymbolic zero first-order variance coordinates are reported without Wald studentization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Algorithms 1--2 and Theorems 5--6 are sound and complete for marginal and conditional counterfactual identification from arbitrary observational and experimental inputs in recursive acyclic SCMs.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The acyclic-reduction theorem uses this as a base case; the present fixed-decoder output-language impossibility is orthogonal and does not refute it.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 9.10 proves soundness of an extended ID algorithm for cyclic ioSCM interventional effects, and Remark 9.11 makes no completeness claim.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The cyclic semantics inform the model setup but do not address fixed-decoder Layer-3 output-language completeness.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2.4 gives finite canonical acyclic SCMs, and the paper reduces counterfactual bounds to polynomial optimization.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Finite response parametrization informs the explicit decoder, but it does not provide rational descent for the source-product image.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Algebraic geometry gives exact feasibility tests and algebraic recovery in selected functional causal structures with two binary observed variables.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The algebraic-branch theorem proves non-representability by rational circuits on a different fixed source-decoder conditional-counterfactual instance.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The inflation hierarchy converges asymptotically to the compatible set for finite latent causal structures.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The compatibility result motivates exact source-aware feasibility tests but does not give a finite rational identifying circuit for every fiber-constant target.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 characterize source-aligned influence functions and canonical gradients for prespecified smooth data-fusion targets.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The circuit-inference theorem uses this only for regular rational outputs; the algebraic obstruction itself has no inference claim.

body.tldr: For each well-typed explicit source-decoder input \(I\), the relevant comparison family is \(\mathfrak M(I):=\{\mathcal M_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_{\mathcal L}\}\), with the decoder and finite source alphabets fixed and only source masses varying.  Uniform conditional-counterfactual identification on this same-instance family does not imply rational-circuit representability: a two-variable legal instance has menu coordinates \(a=xy\), \(b=xz\), \(c=yz\) and identified target \(q=x=\sqrt{ab/c}\).  Therefore no total sound formula-or-same-instance-countermodel procedure with rational positive outputs can be complete; a third result such as \(O\) is unavoidable.  Verified rational formulas and accepted countermodels remain sound, regular returned circuits retain multinomial inference, and universal nonvanishing boundary transmission remains a separate open question.

project_justification.gap: Published acyclic CTFID completeness concerns recursive SCM classes and does not imply completeness of a rational-only output language for a fixed explicit source decoder.  Cyclic simple-SCM semantics and causal-compatibility algorithms likewise do not determine whether a uniformly identified same-instance conditional counterfactual must be rational in the supplied regime probabilities.
project_justification.niche: Finite independent-source decoders expose a distinct algebraic phenomenon: observed regime cells can be pairwise products of source probabilities, while positivity selects a unique algebraic branch that is constant on every legal source fiber but lies outside the rational function field.
project_justification.fill: The note gives an explicit legal same-alphabet instance with \(H=xyz\), \(K=yz\), and \(q=\sqrt{ab/c}\), proves rational non-representability by a field automorphism, and derives an algorithm-independent impossibility theorem for two-outcome rational-formula-or-same-instance-countermodel procedures.  It retains sound verified outputs, isolates universal boundary transmission as a separate open problem, and treats semialgebraic or algebraic output-language completeness only as a future direction.

body.related_work: CorreaLeeBareinboim2021 proves soundness and completeness of CTFID for recursive acyclic SCMs; the present theorem neither contradicts nor narrows that result because it studies a fixed explicit source-decoder family and a rational-only output contract.  BongersForrePetersMooij2021 supplies simple-SCM solvability semantics, and ForreMooij2020 supplies sound cyclic interventional identification without Layer-3 completeness.  LeeSpekkens2017 demonstrates exact algebraic methods in selected small functional structures, while NavascuesWolfe2020 and WolfeSpekkensFritz2019 show that independent sources impose compatibility constraints beyond unrestricted response-table mixtures.  These works motivate an enlarged semialgebraic output language but do not prove its completeness here.  LiLuedtke2023 informs inference for returned regular circuits, and Tikka2023 identifies cfid as the software consumer.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Explicit response and source tables may be exponentially larger than the graph, and no succinct-input efficiency claim is made.  The impossibility theorem is relative to one fixed decoder family \(\mathfrak M(I)\); it does not transfer upward to every mechanism compatible with \(G\).  The permitted edge \(Y\to W\) is inactive in the witness, so cyclic feedback is not load-bearing.  Universal transmission of every local separator through arbitrary stored interfaces remains open, as does any general completeness theorem for semialgebraic or algebraic output languages.  Inference remains fixed-dimensional and pointwise on positive-margin strata.
body.honest_scope: The established headline is an algorithm-independent impossibility for rational positive outputs paired with genuine same-instance negative countermodels.  It is witnessed inside the explicit family \(\mathfrak M(I)=\{\mathcal M_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_{\mathcal L}\}\), not the full class of mechanisms bounded by \(G\), and therefore makes no upward identification claim.  It does not refute published acyclic CTFID completeness.  SC-CTFID termination and one-way output soundness, exact cycle legality, selected source-realizability calculations, conditional boundary gluing, and regular circuit inference remain valid.  The new theorem answers rational descent negatively; the existence of a nonvanishing transmitting exterior assignment for every local separator is retained as its own recursion-specific open question.  Semialgebraic or CAD-based completeness is a proposal only until an explicit piecewise branch or Thom-root language and a proof are supplied.
body.interpretation: The obstruction is representational, not ambiguity within the explicit instance.  The menu determines \(x^2=ab/c\), probability positivity selects the unique branch \(x\geq0\), and every same-instance model in the fiber has the same target; nevertheless a simultaneous sign-flip fixes \(a,b,c\) and excludes \(x\) from \(\mathbb Q(a,b,c)\).  A quantifier-free semialgebraic graph certifies this one branch, but general completeness for semialgebraic separators, piecewise algebraic branches, or Thom-root circuits is open.  Local-to-global nonvanishing transmission is logically separate.
